advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Clarify or extend the runbook's mirror fetch so objects reachable only from refs/changes or refs/meta (not main) can also be imported before the connectivity fsck is trusted.
evidence: ABSENCE: no fetch of refs/changes/* or refs/meta/* — objects unique to those refs are never imported by a main-only fetch
advisory.finding: The repair runbook fetches only refs/heads/main from the mirror (step 3) but the verification (step 5) checks refs/changes and refs/meta; a missing object reachable only from a change ref or meta ref (not from main) would not be imported by the main-only fetch, leaving the connectivity-only fsck able to still report the missing object.
scenarios: The blocked push's missing blob belongs to a change series or NoteDb meta ref rather than to main's history

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the autodeploy source-grep with a behavioral test that runs autodeploy's `changed` gate over a diff touching infra/compose/jgit.config and asserts the config_manual signal is emitted.
evidence: autodeploy.sh:218 comment: '# infra/compose/gerrit.config and infra/compose/jgit.config are in this list'
autodeploy.sh:232 actual gate var: CONFIG_PATHS='... infra/compose/jgit.config infra/scripts/materialize-gerrit-jgit-config.sh'
autodeploy.sh:907-908 the behavior under test: `if changed "$CONFIG_PATHS"; then err config_manual ...` is never exercised
compose-up.sh invokes: bash "${REPO_ROOT}/infra/scripts/materialize-gerrit-jgit-config.sh" "${REPO_ROOT}" "${SITE_HOST_DIR}" "${GERRIT_UID}:${GERRIT_UID}" — its runtime effect is never asserted
advisory.finding: test_autodeploy_flags_jgit_config_for_manual_apply asserts on the TEXT of autodeploy.sh (the unit under test) rather than its behavior. It greps for 'infra/compose/jgit.config' and 'infra/scripts/materialize-gerrit-jgit-config.sh' as substrings; both strings also appear in a comment block (autodeploy.sh:218), so the test passes even if the paths were only commented and NOT present in the actual CONFIG_PATHS variable (autodeploy.sh:232). It never drives the `changed "$CONFIG_PATHS"` gate that emits the config_manual signal, so it cannot detect a regression in the detect-only signalling behavior this diff introduces, and breaks on a behavior-preserving refactor.
merged_from: The second half of test_compose_mounts_and_seeds_jgit_config greps compose-up.sh source text for 'materialize-gerrit-jgit-config.sh' and '"${SITE_HOST_DIR}"' instead of exercising the seeding behavior. This is source-grepping over the executable script under test: it asserts the implementation text, not that jgit.config is materialized into the site etc dir, and breaks on a behavior-preserving refactor (e.g. renaming the local var or inlining the call).
scenarios: A refactor removes jgit.config from CONFIG_PATHS but leaves it in the comment — test stays green while the manual-apply signal is silently lost.
Path is present in a comment only; gate never fires; test still passes.
